subject: Medigen: DPA, SCCs and subprocessor consolidation request
content:
-----Original Message-----
From: Priya Shah <security@medigen.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA, SCCs and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — Medigen is excited to move the pilot forward. Legal and security asked me to consolidate a small set of asks so we can complete our internal risk sign-off. Can you please: 

- Share the most recent DPA with your tracked redlines (we have a few non-negotiables on logging and retention)
- Confirm which SCCs you rely on and whether you can sign the UK IDTA / UK Addendum for our UK-bound workloads
- Provide a current list of subprocessors with the geographic locations of data processing for each (we need to confirm no offshored processing for UK patient data)
- Populate the attached SCCs/TIA matrix with your suggested mitigations and any TIA/DTIA evidence pointers

I attached our questionnaire and an initial redline to your DPA for context. If we can get these items by Friday our procurement schedule stays intact.

Attachments: Medigen_DPA_requests_v1.docx, medigen_questionnaire.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Security Operations
Medigen Therapeutics
security@medigen.com

On Thu, 8 Oct 2026 at 10:22, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
To: Priya Shah <security@medigen.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA, SCCs and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear asks. A quick summary of what we can provide by Friday and outstanding items: 

1) DPA redlines: we will return a tracked-redline version. Most of your non-negotiables (logging controls, access auditability) are already covered in Section 6 and Section 9; we need to confirm retention windows for telemetry logs vs. customer payloads. Suggestion: we can accept a 90-day telemetry retention for aggregated logs but request to keep payload retention aligned with customer-configured retention in Private deployments.

2) SCCs / UK Addendum: Redwood signs the EU SCCs and offers the UK IDTA / UK Addendum as part of our standard enterprise terms. For the pilot we can execute the UK Addendum; however, we need to confirm which environment you plan to use (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private) as that affects subprocessor exposure and TIA scope.

3) Subprocessors and locations: Laura will attach the current subprocessor CSV. Note: a few infra providers handle ephemeral GPU allocation in the US and eu-west-1 for burst capacity; we can document that no UK patient payload will be routed to non-UK jurisdictions if you choose a UK-dedicated deployment.

4) TIAs/DTIAs: we maintain a TIAs matrix per major region. For some infra subprocessors we have completed DTIAs; for others we have compensating controls documented. We will mark items that require a deeper operational evidence handoff.

Deliverables by Friday (EOD): tracked DPA redline (Medigen_DPA_redlines_v2.docx), subprocessor_list_medigen.csv (location column included), SCCs_TIA_matrix.xlsx with our mitigation notes. If you need DocuSign for the Addendum we can route it once redlines are agreed.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Security & Product Trust
Redwood Inference
vivek@redwoodinference.com


On Fri, 9 Oct 2026 at 15:45, Priya Shah <security@medigen.com> wrote:
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, legal@medigen.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA, SCCs and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Thanks Vivek — that sounds workable. A couple quick clarifications before we route internally: 

- For the hosted vs dedicated vs private question: the pilot will start in a hosted environment but must be able to transition to a UK-dedicated deployment in month 2. Can you confirm any lead time for spinning up a UK-dedicated pool and what the migration/data cutover process looks like?
- Can you confirm that any telemetry logs that contain partial payload metadata will be redacted when retained for the 90-day telemetry retention? We need to avoid any patient identifiers in logs stored outside the UK.
- Please include a short paragraph in the SCCs_TIA_matrix.xlsx that states which subprocessors have access to encryption keys or plaintext payloads.

If you can drop the attachments to the Drive link you mentioned (or send via DocuSign for the Addendum), we can get procurement and legal aligned for signature.

Attachments included: none (we will wait for your pack)

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Security Operations
Medigen Therapeutics
security@medigen.com
